[PATH:empirical] Optogenetic manipulation of IT-to-V1 feedback projections in macaques during ambiguous visual tasks, combined with laminar recordings in V1 to measure sub-millisecond response latencies — Directly tests the causal necessity of IT-originating feedback for disambiguation and whether its precision is sub-millisecond, while also comparing effects of V2/V3 feedback perturbation.

[PATH:empirical] High-density electrophysiology in V1 of non-human primates performing a bistable perception task, with cross-correlation and spike-triggered averaging to distinguish feedback from IT vs. V2/V3 based on latency and temporal jitter — Provides evidence for the claimed dual time-scale feedback and whether only the fastest IT-originating component correlates with perceptual switches.

[PATH:theoretical] Biophysically detailed spiking network model of V1 with feedback from IT and V2/V3, constrained by known anatomy, to test whether sub-millisecond IT feedback is necessary and sufficient for disambiguation under ambiguous input — Evaluates the plausibility and necessity of the proposed hierarchical gating mechanism in silico, and can identify conditions under which the hypothesis fails.
